overview: Early blight is a common fungal disease of tomato plants caused by Alternaria solani. It can affect leaves, stems, and fruit, and typically starts as small dark brown spots on older leaves.
symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern) on older leaves.
Leaves turn yellow and drop off as the disease progresses.
Leathery black spots near the stem end of fruits.
organicTreatments: Spray copper fungicide (certified organic) at the first sign of disease.
Apply 2% Neem Oil spray once every 10 days to control spore germination.
Prune lower leaves to reduce soil splash and improve air circulation.
chemicalTreatments: Mancozeb 75% WP (2 g/L of water) sprayed at 10-14 day intervals.
Chlorothalonil 75% WP (1.5-2 g/L of water) as a protective cover spray.
preventiveMeasures: Practice 3-year crop rotation (avoid nightshade family crops).
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead watering to keep foliage dry.
Apply thick organic mulch to prevent fungal spores from splashing up from the soil.
progressionInfo: In warm, humid weather (24-29°C), spots can enlarge rapidly. Without treatment, complete defoliation can occur within 14-21 days, causing severe yield loss.

overview: Late blight is a highly destructive fungal-like oomycete disease. It thrives in cool, wet weather and can destroy an entire crop field within days if left unchecked.
symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked spots on leaves that rapidly turn dark brown or black.
White fuzzy growth on the undersides of affected leaves during humid mornings.
Large, firm, greasy golden-brown spots on green and ripe fruits.
organicTreatments: Destroy and burn all infected crop residue; do not compost.
Apply copper octanoate or copper hydroxide spray immediately.
Use bio-fungicide sprays based on Bacillus subtilis (10g/L).
chemicalTreatments: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (2.5 g/L of water) as systemic-contact control.
Azoxystrobin 23% SC (1 ml/L of water) at the early stage of infection.
preventiveMeasures: Ensure proper spacing to encourage quick drying of leaves.
Avoid fields where late blight was reported in potato crops recently.
progressionInfo: Thrives in temperatures between 15-21°C with high relative humidity. Under optimal conditions, it can spread to the entire field within 3 to 7 days.

overview: Early blight affects potato foliage, reducing photosynthetic area and leading to smaller tuber sizes. It appears initially on older, mature leaves.
symptoms: Small, dark, concentric-ring spots on lower leaves.
Leaves turn yellow and dry up, starting from bottom of the plant.
Dark, sunken, circular lesions on harvested potato tubers.
organicTreatments: Apply copper-based sprays early in the season.
Utilize Trichoderma harzianum soil treatment during planting.
Irrigate early in the morning so leaves dry quickly during the day.
chemicalTreatments: Propineb 70% WP (2 g/L of water) at first symptoms.
Difenoconazole 25% EC (0.5 ml/L of water) for curative action.
preventiveMeasures: Maintain adequate soil nitrogen levels (stressed plants are more susceptible).
Harvest tubers only after complete vine death to prevent skin wounding.
progressionInfo: Can result in yield reductions of 20-30% if defoliation occurs during the tuber bulking stage.

overview: Late blight is the historical cause of the Irish Potato Famine. It remains one of the most critical threats to global potato farming, destroying both leaves and tubers.
symptoms: Dark brown, water-soaked lesions starting at leaf tips and margins.
Fuzzy white mold appearing on the lower surface of leaves under wet conditions.
Tubers exhibit reddish-brown dry rot extending into the flesh.
organicTreatments: Spray copper oxide/hydroxide protective mixtures repeatedly during rainy periods.
Immediately rogue out and destroy infected plants to limit spore travel.
chemicalTreatments: Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (2.5 g/L of water) at weekly intervals.
Dimethomorph 50% WP (1 g/L of water) mixed with contact fungicide.
preventiveMeasures: Keep potato tubers well hilled/covered with soil to shield them from washing spores.
Monitor local weather forecasts for cold, rainy warnings and spray beforehand.
Destroy cull piles (discarded potatoes) which serve as primary inoculum sources.
progressionInfo: Under high humidity (>90%) and cool temperatures (15-20°C), spores can destroy a healthy potato field in under 5 days.

overview: Rice Blast is a significant threat to global food security. It can affect all aboveground parts of the rice plant, including leaves, collars, nodes, and panicles.
symptoms: Spindle-shaped (diamond) spots on leaves with reddish-brown borders and grey centers.
Rotting of the neck (stem right below panicle), causing the heads to break off (neck blast).
organicTreatments: Treat seeds with Pseudomonas fluorescens formulation (10g/kg of seeds).
Apply silicon-rich fertilizers or rice husk ash to strengthen cell walls.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization, which soft-tissue builds plants.
chemicalTreatments: Tricyclazole 75% WP (0.6 g/L of water) - highly effective for neck blast prevention.
Isoprothiolane 40% EC (1.5 ml/L of water) at tillering and panicle initiation.
preventiveMeasures: Avoid continuous flooding; adopt intermittent alternate wetting and drying.
Use blast-resistant rice varieties recommended for the region.
Burn or plow under stubble after harvest to eliminate overwintering spores.
progressionInfo: Neck blast infection right after flowering is most critical, potentially causing 80-100% crop loss in a short period.

overview: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) is a major bacterial disease of rice, causing severe drying of leaves and structural wilting (known as kresek).
symptoms: Yellow to white wavy stripes starting from leaf tips and running down leaf margins.
Milky or cloudy bacterial droplets oozing from cut leaves on humid mornings.
Systemic wilting of young seedlings (kresek phase) where leaves roll up and die.
organicTreatments: Spray Fresh Cow Dung Extract (5%) filtered slurry to stimulate local resistance.
Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens solution (20 g/L) weekly.
Drain fields temporarily if the infection starts spreading rapidly.
chemicalTreatments: Streptocycline (antibiotic) (0.1 g/L of water) mixed with Copper Oxychloride (2 g/L).
preventiveMeasures: Avoid clipping seedling tips before transplanting (reduces bacterial entry points).
Use balanced NPK fertilizer ratio; avoid high dosage of Nitrogen.
Ensure proper field drainage; do not allow deep standing water in nursery.
progressionInfo: Kresek phase in young plants leads to complete death of the tillers. Foliage damage in mature crops blocks grain filling, causing up to 50% yield loss.
